notes: DNSenum automates DNS enumeration: NS record discovery, MX enumeration, AXFR attempts against all nameservers, and subdomain brute force - all in one run. Outputs clean results and can save to XML. Covers in one command what would require separate dig commands for NS, MX, SOA, AXFR, and brute force. Use --dnsserver to target a specific internal DNS server (critical in lab environments). -p 0 -s 0 disables Google scraping/Bing scraping (noise/accuracy concerns). Chaining: dnsenum as comprehensive first-pass DNS → review AXFR if successful → brute-forced subdomains become new scan targets → feed IPs to nmap. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 6 (Information Gathering).

references.title: OffSec PEN-200 - Penetration Testing with Kali Linux

recommended.note: Run WHOIS first to identify registrar, nameservers, and registered IPs.
After enumerating subdomains, run nmap against discovered hosts.
Discovered IPs may expose SNMP - scan UDP 161 next.

defense.why_it_works: DNS zone transfers (AXFR) are a legitimate replication mechanism - if not restricted to authorised secondary nameservers, any host can request a full dump of the zone. Subdomain brute force succeeds when domains resolve valid hosts that are not publicly advertised.
defense.prerequisites: DNS server reachable on UDP/TCP 53. AXFR requires the target nameserver to allow zone transfers from the attacker's IP (misconfigured allow-transfer).
defense.misconfiguration: Zone transfer unrestricted: `allow-transfer { any; };` in named.conf allows any IP to enumerate all records in the zone.
defense.impact: Full internal DNS record dump reveals hostnames, internal IP addresses, mail servers, and service locations - dramatically accelerates reconnaissance.
defense.detection: AXFR requests visible in DNS server query logs (type=AXFR from unexpected source IPs). Subdomain brute force produces high NXDOMAIN rates from a single source IP.
defense.artifacts: DNS server query logs, firewall connection logs on TCP/UDP 53.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=dns sourcetype="stream:dns"
| stats count count(eval(reply_code=\"NXDOMAIN\")) as nx by src_ip, bin(_time, 1m)
| where count>50 OR nx>30
defense.sentinel_kql:
DnsEvents
| summarize queries=count(), nx=countif(ResultCode == 3) by ClientIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where queries > 50 or nx > 30
| sort by queries desc
// dnsenum full enumeration (AXFR attempt + subdomain brute)
defense.sigma_rules: net_dns_enumeration (dnsenum full enumeration (AXFR attempt + subdomain brute))
defense.prevention: Restrict AXFR with allow-transfer to known secondary server IPs. Implement TSIG for zone-transfer authentication. Use split-horizon DNS so internal records are not resolvable externally.
defense.evasion: Slow the brute force request rate; source from multiple IPs to avoid per-IP NXDOMAIN rate limiting.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review DNS logs for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Runs full automated DNS enumeration in one command:
  dnsenum --dnsserver <nameserver>   query this NS
  --enum -p 0 -s 0                   preset without whois page/scrape steps
  -o <outfile> -f <wordlist>         save output; brute-force subdomains from the wordlist
  <domain>                           target
Discovers NS/MX/SOA records, attempts AXFR against every nameserver, and brute-forces subdomains together - a one-shot DNS map.
